narrator.name: Keith Singery
narrator.role: Host, Bittensor Guru podcast; validator operator; Chief Evangelist, TAO.com (Tensora) from March 2025
narrator.one_line: Host of the Bittensor Guru, the longest-running subnet-by-subnet interview podcast in the ecosystem, who ran the sixth-largest validator until it became the TAO.com validator in March 2025 and now speaks as TAO.com's Chief Evangelist.

statements.quote: The Bittensor Guru focuses on Bittensor, the project that combines artificial intelligence and blockchain technology to create an incentivized marketplace for machine learning. This podcast covers the Bittensor ecosystem, community, projects, developments and much more. Hosted by Keith Singery, a Bittensor enthusiast who runs a validator and volunteers as a moderator on the project's official Discord server.
statements.context: The standing show description he wrote for the podcast when it launched on Apple Podcasts and Libsyn in late 2023; the same text is still carried by every directory.

source.title: Bittensor Guru show description
source.outlet: Bittensor Guru (Listen Notes and Apple Podcasts listing)

positioning.category.summary: Bittensor is an incentivized marketplace for machine learning, a project that combines AI and blockchain; he keeps the foundation's marketplace frame rather than coining his own.

relationship.summary: He speaks as an enthusiast who runs a validator and moderates the official Discord, then from March 2025 as the host whose validator became the TAO.com validator and whose show relays TAO.com's subnet evaluations.

audience.summary: He addresses the community and would-be miners subnet by subnet, translating each project into a one-line hook and, at the end of 2025, telling listeners anyone can now mine on hardware they already own.

messaging.proof.summary: His evidence is scale and pedigree: teams that brought 150 million users to AI, a subnet past 1000 GPUs, a subnet cracking the top 15, a permissionless training cluster.

value.functional.summary: The concrete benefit is always a working subnet: a trading competition, a yield engine, decentralised infrastructure, AutoML, zkML, distributed training.

opportunity.summary: He expects deregistration to prune weak subnets and then an explosion of new ones, and reads distributed training and AI coding subnets as the network's big swings.

positioning.differentiator.summary: What is most Bittensor-like to him is open source models, wide-open winner-take-all competition and permissionless mining, summed up as code is intelligence.

foundation.values.summary: He praises subnets for increasing decentralisation and, in a hosts' paraphrase, treats price charts as a distraction next to what holders and builders do.

language.term.summary: He coins Bittensory as an adjective for a subnet that embodies the network's design.

voice.summary: Boosterish, slangy and personal: we're back baby, on a tear, jam on all things 62, code is intelligence man.

value.self_expressive.summary: Being into the most Bittensory subnet signals being a true believer in open, winner-take-all competition.

coinages.meaning: Adjective for a subnet that fully embodies Bittensor's design: open source, wide open, winner-take-all, permissionless mining.
His slogan for why an AI coding subnet is the purest expression of a network that pays for intelligence.

genealogy.summary: From the show's launch in late 2023 he frames Bittensor with the foundation's own words, an incentivized marketplace for machine learning, and speaks as a validator and Discord moderator [keith-singery-001]. His episode copy sells the network one subnet at a time, by team pedigree and scale [keith-singery-002, keith-singery-008], and he reads deregistration as pruning before an explosion of subnets [keith-singery-004].

After his validator became the TAO.com validator he speaks as an evangelist relaying subnet evaluations [keith-singery-013, keith-singery-014]. The register gets louder and more partisan, picking Ridges as the most Bittensory subnet and coining code is intelligence [keith-singery-017, keith-singery-018], and by December 2025 the pitch to listeners is that anyone can mine on hardware they already own [keith-singery-021].
genealogy.shift: From neutral host and validator to affiliated evangelist; from marketplace framing to open-competition slogans; the pruning expectation becomes a hosts' paraphrase that deregistration will shred 40 to 50 subnets [keith-singery-019].

relations.note: Names Ridges the most Bittensory subnet and gives it a full episode.
Both pick Ridges as the proof case in the same quarter; Sami's Ridges memo appeared on 2025-09-23.
Relays Macrocosmos' IOTA launch as the moment anyone can mine.
